keyFindings.description: Security[untrusted-input] hardening: the anchor's comments say an agent's tool-argument line `never matches`; true for the compacted args field, but summarize prints decoded strings (toolName, error.message, extension_error.error) through one log.Print, so a `\u000a` in one of them splits a frame into a second log line beginning wherever it says, and OMP's own stderr reaches the container log unframed (shim.go:381; the tester's recorded risk). The outcome assertion reads `codegraph status` (:3661-3663), so a forged line can misattribute the note or fail the checkpoint, never pass it over an unbuilt index. Not a gate; strip control characters where the summary is printed and soften the comments (Fast-follow h).

refreshWarmLease three-states the read but still drops os.Chtimes's error, as the pre-PR code did: six consecutive write failures on the volume would age a live lease past 60 s with no log line. Pre-existing behaviour; hardening (log once on the first failure) in Fast-follow h.

The evidence filter keeps only `[legion] codegraph warm-up for ` lines, so a failed build's `codegraph init failed for …` line never reaches codegraph-warm-up.txt and a 600 s timeout is not diagnosable from the file the fail line names (the pod log still has it). risks: The live stage 4b repository-tools checkpoint reading the success line from the pod's log is LEGION-578's operator lane; neither proof ran it.

At worker_stop_timeout_seconds: 9 the stop budget has no slack (MinStopGrace = 5 s + 1 s + 3 s exactly): an agent ignoring SIGTERM for the full 5 s plus a warm-up not back within the 3 s floor ends at the launcher's SIGKILL instant; bounded — the lease is left regardless in that case, and stopWarm runs at the SIGTERM relay so the warm-up ends 2–3 s in, in practice.
The checkpoint reads the current container instance's log; a container restarted before repository-tools would never log the line again. No restart precedes it in stage 4b today.

One spurious Chtimes of a successor's lease in the read/Chtimes window remains possible (bounded by one heartbeat); a build exiting 0 as its context ends logs the `ended with its process` line instead of the success line.
